newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Saddam Hussein offers pardon for spies.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Saddam Hussein offers pardon for spies.

text.p: Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein will pardon spies giving themselves up during the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, Iraqi newspapers reported on Thursday.
They said Saddam also instructed that all who confessed would be allowed to keep the money they had made from their spying activities.

The newspapers reported that Saddam had been prompted to offer the amnesty after watching on Iraqi television members of two espionage rings confess to spying for the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and the Israeli Mossad.
Iraqi television on Wednesday showed three Iraqis who confessed to spying for the Israeli intelligence service Mossad.

Last month the television also showed four others who admitted to working for the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency. The United States and Israel dismissed Iraqi claims to have smashed CIA or Mossad spy rings.
The newspapers said the pardon would go into effect on Thursday. It was not clear whether the amnesty would cover members of the two spy networks.

"President Saddam Hussein has seen what has been broadcast by Baghdad television and Shebabb T.V. station...and has decided to pardon in a full and comprehensive manner anyone who committed the crime of submitting information or making contacts with foreign parties," the papers said.
Spies are rarely pardoned in Iraq and they usually receive harsh punishment. Saddam admitted that his amnesty fell "outside the norms which the revolution has been practising".

"President Saddam Hussein, while taking this decision, apologises to noble Iraqi men and women who preserved the covenant...and kisses their heads and hopes they understand the motives behind this decision," the papers said quoting a presidential statement issued late on Wednesday.
The statement said that Saddam took the decision "to provide an opportunity, even to the worst people, to abandon the path of wrongdoing and falsehood", the Iraqi news agency INA reported.
